grouping_rule: Same frozen source path plus same semantic standing only.
items: Falsification document presents CTC as a scientific/falsifiable hypothesis about reality-driven adaptive-mechanism change.
Primary falsifiers test unlimited novelty with fixed mathcal G, environment-independent expansion, and fixed topology matching CTC outcomes.
Source explicitly states mathcal G is not directly observable.
Candidate proxies and experiments use strategy/architecture changes, counterfactual reachability, controlled permeability/feedback/self-modification and mechanism diversity.
Weak CTC uses partial mathcal G_(t+1)/partial Omega_t>0; strong CTC requires Omega->Delta mathcal G with measurable causal contribution.
CTC-active systems are predicted eventually to outperform state/knowledge-only adaptive systems.
CTC does not claim all intelligence needs self-modification, complexity implies openness, self-improvement guarantees open-endedness, or every adaptive system becomes evolutionary.
CTC is proposed necessary for genuine recursive open-ended adaptation and falsified by unlimited adaptation with Delta mathcal G=0.
Implementation roadmap seeks smallest environment testing constraint/reality permeability effects on recursive adaptation.

Implementation philosophy isolates CTC as causal variable; environment supplies changing constraints; metrics cover performance/adaptation/mechanism growth/dependency/removal; staged roadmap moves toy->benchmark->RL/evolutionary systems.
Planned architecture Environment->E*/Omega->C_rev->mathcal G->Agent with closed vs E*-accessible revision branches.
Representation updates alone do not satisfy CTC.
E* carries environmental information, C_rev governs future improvement/search updates, and mathcal G denotes reachable adaptive mechanisms.
Closed mode expected short-term optimization/limited novelty; CTC mode expected stronger shift adaptation, mechanism discovery, lower dependency and preserved reality access.
Falsification controls extra information, compute, data, parameters and adaptation budget and asks whether E* access expands mechanisms or improves future adaptation.
Operational boundary asks E* rightsquigarrow C_rev: yes=adaptive lineage, no=internally generated trajectory.
Related-concepts document positions CTC as a proposed structural condition rather than replacement for adjacent fields.

Source maps CTC to evolution, reinforcement learning, self-modifying AI, open-ended evolution, alignment/corrigibility, control theory and causal inference through the question of whether reality reaches future-change mechanisms.
Information input alone is distinguished from adaptive-mechanism transformation.
CTC rejects complexity/performance/computation/self-modification/novelty-alone definitions and proposes Omega->Delta mathcal G as the deeper property.
Simulator architecture intends to compare fixed, closed-self-modifying and CTC-active systems for long-term adaptive advantage.
Simulator architecture centers Environment->Omega/E*->C_rev->mathcal G->Agent and three adaptation modes, with capability/adaptation/mechanism/transfer/dependency metrics.
Defines simulator modules/environment state and layered agent containing X, K, mathcal G and C_rev.
Simulator loop applies environment constraint, CTC evaluation and updates; minimal prototype file plan is specified.
Closed systems may match short-term performance; CTC systems are predicted to outperform long-term.
Research question proposes open-ended intelligence requires reality access to future-adaptation mechanisms.
figures/ctc_overview.png is actually UTF-8 textual/ASCII/Markdown content despite its extension.
Text diagram contrasts fixed adaptation inside a fixed possibility space with recursive adaptation that changes the possibility space.
CTC transition is defined by reality changing the mechanism generating future changes, not merely causing system change.
